achievements.0: Designed and implemented a critical alarm monitoring system in an IoT environment, processing +500k monthly events, integrating business rules and automated notifications — reducing undetected critical failures by 80% and decreasing average response time from 3–5 hours to ~20 minutes.
achievements.1: Redesigned the MSSQL database architecture to a model optimized for hierarchical data and restructured the backend to operate on the new structure, reducing average complex query time from 2m10s to 35s (~73% reduction) and improving heavy operation performance by up to 4×.
achievements.2: Developed and documented integrations between legacy systems for managing locations, machines, and inspection points and the IoT platform, creating REST APIs that process +2 million records/month. The solution eliminated discrepancies between databases, ensured real-time synchronization (<1s) and increased operational data reliability by >95%.
achievements.3: Implemented two critical telemetry pipelines, integrating Dynapredict and PI System, supporting +10k measurements/hour, with dynamic ID mapping, duplicate filtering, batch formatting, and resilient sending via APIs. The solution increased successful delivery rate to 99.8%, reduced ingestion failures by >90%, and enabled complete monitoring via Prometheus.

todoManager.title: TodoManager — Demand Planning
todoManager.description: Full stack application that orchestrates Latinhas LLC's production planning, combining an Express + Prisma API documented in OpenAPI with a responsive Next.js interface ready for corporate use.
highlights: Frontend in Next.js 14 with React Hook Form, TanStack Query, and native dark mode.
Modular backend in Express 4 + Prisma 5, centralized validations, structured logging, and public OpenAPI for partner squads.
Complete CRUD for demands and SKUs with validations, pagination, and cascade deletion.
Containerized integration with Docker and pipeline ready for multiple environments.
todoManager.imageAlt: Animated demonstration of TodoManager showing the demand flow

restora.title: Restora — Landing Page
restora.description: Cosmetics brand landing page developed with a focus on user experience, consistent visual identity, and high performance.
highlights: Developed with Next.js 15, leveraging the framework's latest features for low Time to First Byte (TTFB) latencies.
Modern and responsive design, resulting in a more fluid and optimized navigation.
Conversion-optimized interface, seeking to optimize dwell time and reduce bounce rate.
Fully responsive architecture, ensuring loading below 1.2s in 98% of tested resolutions.
restora.imageAlt: Animated demonstration of the Restora landing page showing the natural cosmetics brand's visual identity

genericRestClient.title: GenericRestClient - Generic HTTP REST client
genericRestClient.description: Generic REST client for .NET 9.0 with support for authentication, rate limiting, and automatic retry. Developed as a solution for integrating with REST APIs in a resilient and configurable way.
highlights: Flexible authentication with support for Bearer Token, OAuth2 (with automatic refresh) and API Key via header or query string.
Configurable rate limiting with requests per minute control, automatic queue, and handling of exceeded limits.
Intelligent automatic retry for 429 and 5xx codes, with support for Retry-After header and configurable exponential or linear backoff.
Robust resilience using Polly for automatic handling of transient failures (timeout, DNS, etc.) and complete HTTP operations (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE).
genericRestClient.imageAlt: Demonstration of GenericRestClient showing authentication, rate limiting, and automatic retry features

nextRenderLab.title: NextRenderLab — Rendering Strategies
nextRenderLab.description: Educational project demonstrating different Next.js rendering strategies with practical and interactive examples, exploring CSR, SSR, SSG, ISR, and hybrid approaches.
highlights: Practical demonstration of five main strategies: CSR, SSR, SSG, ISR, and Hybrid with interactive examples and visualizations.
Developed with Next.js 16 (App Router), React 19, and TypeScript 5, leveraging the latest features of the ecosystem.
Each page demonstrates a specific strategy with technical information, rendering flows, and practical use cases.
Modern interface with Tailwind CSS 4, providing a clear and intuitive educational experience to understand when to use each approach.
nextRenderLab.imageAlt: Demonstration of NextRenderLab showing different Next.js rendering strategies
